kind: analyze (classical Monte Carlo sweep of the CrN Heisenberg model -> normalised staggered-magnetisation curve M(T)/M(0) and the Neel temperature)
provenance: truth copied from 3_reproduction/L7/result.json (runs.A.T_grid_K, runs.A.M_stag_norm, ground_truth.T_N_K), produced by 3_reproduction/L7/auditor/fit_neel.py on the run-A VAMPIRE outputs. reviewer/make_reference.py recomputes both answers from the STAGED agent/mc_sweep.csv alone and agrees with result.json to 4.8e-7 per curve point and 2e-4 K on T_N (verified 2026-09-06).
order_parameter_definition: M(T) = mean over the two Cr sublattices (VAMPIRE materials 0 and 1) of output:material-mean-magnetisation-LENGTH -- the mean of the per-configuration sublattice-moment MAGNITUDE, not the magnitude of the time-averaged vector -- seed-averaged over the three seeds and normalised by its value at the lowest grid temperature (T = 0 K). With zero anisotropy the Neel axis diffuses, so |<m>| decays while <|m|> does not; choosing between them is the tested skill and is NOT pinned by the prompt.
T_N_definition: single free parameter of M(T)/M(0) = (1 - T/T_N)^(1/3), exponent fixed at 1/3 and M(0) pinned to the measured T = 0 value, fitted over the points with M/M(0) in [0.10, 0.60] (13 points). The estimator is NOT pinned by the prompt: the mean-sublattice longitudinal susceptibility peak gives 284.099 K and the alternative fit windows 284.247 K, all far inside the +/-10% band.

M_stag_norm.rule: PRIMARY, handbook 2(2) per-point curve rule: |sub_i - truth_i| <= max(0.10*|truth_i|, floor) with floor = 0.10 (= 0.10 * max|truth| = 0.10 * 1.0, the curve's characteristic scale, so this is the standard 2(2) floor written out, not an exception). One entry per grid temperature in ASCENDING temperature order; a list of any other length is a gating failure (score 0 before any primary check).
M_stag_norm.note: The floor makes the tail (T >= 290 K, truth < 0.10) effectively ungraded. Accepted: every curve point, including the transition region, has the same +/-0.10 absolute band. Seed-to-seed scatter on this curve is at most 0.020 (single-seed vs seed-averaged), so a single-seed answer passes by design.

estimator_spread_K.note: Checked estimators include 280 K and 282.5 K independent readings and the 284.213 K reference; they lie inside the approved 10% band. The +/-10% standard tolerance therefore accepts the whole family without a documented exception.

secondary.note: Recorded in the grading report, NOT scored (handbook 1(2)).

normalisation_at_T0.rule: SECONDARY: the first entry should be 1.000 (the curve is normalised at the lowest grid temperature). A curve reported in muB fails the primary curve check anyway (2.850 vs 1.000).

monotonic_decrease.rule: SECONDARY: M(T)/M(0) should not rise with T beyond seed scatter. Recorded as a flag; the per-point primary match already enforces the shape.

T_N_vs_chi_peak_K.rule: SECONDARY: our independent mean-sublattice longitudinal susceptibility peak, 0.11 K from the fit. Recorded for context.

score: 1 only if BOTH primary checks pass: the 43-point curve per-point match and the T_N scalar band. Either failure scores 0 (binary all-primary-pass, handbook 1(1)). A missing field, a non-numeric entry, or a curve of the wrong length scores 0 as a gating failure.
